gen-dafont-origami-gf-pt-sans-caption: Unique is the word for Origami, a brush-drawn single stroke that looks poured. PT Sans Caption does the quieter job, with big-bodied lowercase and bowls left inviting, while the heading handles all the attitude.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-puritan: Origami builds every letter from one width of stroke, like a sign-painter's brush dragged steadily across. Puritan follows in rounded, open forms and oversized e and a counters, so a size a step or two below the heading feels natural.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-questrial: Origami's lowercase has the dense, poured-lead mass of type cast in a hurry. And Questrial, a flat sans with a tall band of letters, does the opposite job: the heading grabs attention, while the body simply lets the words through.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-radio-canada: Brush-drawn at constant width, Origami feels like a sign painter's single sweep. Radio Canada's steady, pressure-free line and clearly opened curve endings give it a strength of its own: a plain sans that stays crisp beside such a loud partner.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-radio-canada-big: Radio Canada Big reads like a sans-serif with its sleeves rolled up, with terminals finishing clear of the stem and an x-height filling the line. Origami's brushy heading keeps it company without crowding.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-readex-pro: Brush-stroke boldness, then a tidy follow-up. Readex Pro brings broad gaps at the terminals and a steady weight from word to word, and that makes a stretch of text feel unhurried beside Origami's lead-type mass.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-roboto: Roboto brings generous mouths on its round letters, leaving little to fuss over. Origami has no thin strokes to vanish in glare, just a constant brush line, so the heading holds its own while the sans-serif body keeps everything moving along.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-ruda: Approachable is how Ruda feels, with a sizable x-height and wide-mouthed rounds in a wire-like monoline. And Origami's single-stroke brush heading gives the page its personality, leaving this plain sans to carry the text.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-saira: Glass-tube lettering, hollow and constant. Saira's see-through s and rounded letters stretching high make a sans-serif body that shrinks Origami's drama if the heading is set small, so give the heading room.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-sarpanch: Cord-thick curves, as heavy as the stems. Sarpanch is a plain sans with a clearly open lowercase e and a compact gap up to the ascenders, so text settles into an easy rhythm under Origami.
